design_references.work: Yamaguchi, Golde, Arp & Rieck (2014), Code Property Graphs, IEEE S&P
design_references.applied: Statement nodes joined by control-flow and dependence edges, so queries can span syntax, flow and data dependence at once.
The export ships derived-view Cypher and validation Cypher so the graph can be extended without changing the extractor.

design_references.work: Lehnert, A review of software change impact analysis
design_references.applied: Blind spots are exported as nodes; no automated impact analysis is complete and the graph says so.
Column, Statement and Parameter are nodes because each takes part in several independent relationships; relationship properties minimised.

supported_questions.question: What breaks if I change a given column?
Which business rules apply to a program unit, table or column?
Where does a given rule live in the source?
Which program units read or write a given table?
What is the calling interface of a program unit?
Which rules still need a person to confirm them?
Which rules are recorded but not enforced by the database?
Which program units are most complex?
Which columns are used most widely?
Which tables are never touched by any program unit?
What open questions remain for the business?
What can this graph NOT see?

concepts.name: Hot column
concepts.purpose: A column read or written by more than two program units — change last.

concepts.name: Rule-bearing statement
concepts.purpose: A statement that implements at least one business rule.

concepts.name: Write path
concepts.purpose: Statements on a control-flow path that ends in a write.

constraints.name: Every rule traces to source
constraints.purpose: A rule with no program unit and no table cannot be verified.

constraints.name: No orphan columns in rules
constraints.purpose: A rule constraining a column that does not exist indicates a join error.

constraints.name: Unenforced constraints are visible
constraints.purpose: Any rule the database does not enforce must be flagged for review.

blind_spots.detail: 0 dynamic SQL block(s). Tables and columns referenced only in strings assembled at runtime are invisible to static analysis.
Schedulers, screens, batch wrappers and other systems that invoke these objects are outside the analysed source, so no inbound edge exists.
0 call(s) to routines outside this codebase. Their effects are unknown and absent from the graph.
Database triggers fire on DML without an explicit call edge; any such effect is not represented as a dependency.
